title: Asset Manifest
description:
Every asset the game needs, its source, its cost, and its status.

This is an ARTIFACT, not a stage. There is deliberately no asset-production state: serializing art behind a gate would put code behind art and wreck a 7-14 day schedule. Asset work happens inside prototype and production, tracked here as line-item status, and `complete` becomes a guard on production exit.

It is authored during design because asset cost is an input to the scope decision — and an input cannot be produced downstream of the decision it feeds.

source.description: Drives both cost and licensing risk. Library and procedural are the cheap paths and should be preferred at this scale.

license.description: Required before a purchased or library asset can be integrated. An unlicensed asset in a published build is a real liability, not a paperwork detail.

pipeline.description: How source assets become runtime assets. 3D adds compression steps that materially change load time on mobile web.

complete.description: True when every non-cut item is integrated. Part of the content_complete guard on production exit — which is why CONTENT COMPLETE is not a lifecycle state.
